accuracy.evidence: Zero as the number of an empty set and the step before 1 when counting back matches Development Matters (2021) Reception Mathematics (count objects, say how many, link numerals to amounts), White Rose Maths Reception 'Alive in 5: introducing zero' and NCETM Mastering Number counting back to 0. Scenes checked by hand: plates of 3 and 4 biscuits empty to 0 and only the 0 key is accepted; boxes 0,1,0,3,0,2 sort to none x3 and some x3; 4 frogs count back 3,2,1,0; nests 2,0,3,1 take cards 2,0,3,1; track gaps 0,3,5 take cards 0,3,5. Parameterised answers n-n and n*0 give 0 at n = 1, 3, 5 and 2, 3, 5.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the zero slips documented by Anthony and Walshaw (2004, 'Zero: a none number?') and named in the adult text: counting the container (plate key 1 feedback, empty-nest card feedback, m1, m7, challenge 'plate'), zero as 'no number' or blank (frogs predict, p3, m8, challenge 'nothing'), stopping at 1 when counting back (frogs predict and feedback, m2, challenge 'back'), 1 tiny thing called none (boxes predict, p4, m4, challenge 'one'), and 0 placed after 5 or 9 as on a keypad (track predict and gap feedback, m5, challenge 'end').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagzero is about the empty set and the count-back step to 0: biscuits disappear one tap at a time with the count shown beside the plate until the plate is bare, bead boxes split into empty and some, frogs leave a log one at a time with the count-back trail 4, 3, 2, 1, 0 written in the banner, a nest with no eggs needs the 0 card, and a 0-5 track has its first gap before 1. No scene works for another number topic by changing labels, because each one turns on reaching or placing none.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child reaches zero by doing: the number keys refuse an answer until the plate is empty, then accept only 0; the frogs scene will not let a frog jump until the child says how many are left, so the count-back is spoken at every step down to 0. Wrong answers name the slip ('1 is the plate', 'that is how many there were', 'counting back goes 2, 1, 0'), and the done messages confirm the rule only after the child has found it.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'Yes, it is nearly empty' for a box with 1 bead (it only sorts into Some), 'Nothing, counting stops at 1' (the last frog leaves and 0 is the answer), 'No card, it is empty' for the empty nest (the 0 card fits it) and 'After 5, at the end' for zero on the track (the end gap rejects 0 with 'zero comes just before 1').

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with wrong options tagged to five messages: plate (count what is on it, not the plate), nothing (zero is a real number we say and write), one (1 is still some), back (counting back goes 3, 2, 1, then 0) and end (0 comes just before 1, it is the smallest). The answer order rotates each question so the right answer is not always first.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences, numbers up to 3 and things a 4-year-old has handled (biscuits, frogs, beads); each lab prompt gives one action. Curriculum terms (empty set, Development Matters, count back) stay in the adult text. The validator's readability limits for kid and adult text pass.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: eating down to zero, counting back past 1, counting the plate, one bead is some and 0 comes first. Adult paragraphs: curriculum placement, a grapes-and-cards activity, five named mistakes, what each lab scene does. No stock phrases; the content gate's filler and 12% duplicate checks pass.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark: the plate fills about 60% of the width with biscuits big enough to tap, the six 0-5 number keys are about 50 px wide and 58 px tall, bead boxes sit in a 3 x 2 grid under two tall bins, four nests fit one row with eggs spaced so 3 can be counted, and the 6-cell track fits with nothing clipped. The iPhone 13 walkthrough completes every Show me.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Eat a biscuit and number keys 0-5 (biscuits left), each box to None or Some, A frog jumps plus number keys (frogs on the log), Pick card then Put it on nest N (with its egg count), and Pick card then Put it in the gap before 1 or after N. The canvas aria-label reports each count and verdict; axe WCAG 2.1 AA runs clean in light and dark themes.
